prompt: On January 12, 2026, Atty. D agreed to prepare and to give not later than January 30, 2026, 50 questions for the first preboard examination, being prepared by Atty. V, where there will be 100 questions. The examination will be administered on February 7, 2026. Which of the following statements is not correct?

choices.text: The agreement need not be in writing to be enforceable
The agreement is valid, hence Atty. V can ask Atty. D for specific performance
The agreement is without effect because its fulfillment depends upon the sole will of Atty. D
The contract is enforceable hence, Atty. D incurs delay if he cannot prepare and give the 50 questions on January 30, 2026

rationale: The undertaking to prepare and submit 50 questions is a pure obligation to do (a personal service), not a suspensive condition dependent on the debtor's sole will. Art. 1182 voids only conditional obligations whose fulfillment depends purely on the debtor's whim/will — it does not apply to a straightforward service obligation, so statement (c) mischaracterizes the contract and is the incorrect one.

prompt: If the right of the creditor to enforce his claim against the debtor has prescribed and yet a third person effected the payment which was accepted by the creditor, which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: The third person cannot recover from the creditor the amount paid because the creditor was benefited.
The third person cannot recover from the debtor the amount paid to the creditor
The third person can recover from the third person the amount paid if the third person is not aware that there was prescription
The third person can no longer recover from either the creditor or debtor because he voluntarily effected

rationale: Once a debt has prescribed, it survives only as a natural obligation that authorizes the creditor to retain what is voluntarily paid (Art. 1423). Since the debt was no longer legally enforceable, the debtor derived no real 'benefit' from the third person's payment, so under Art. 1236 the third person cannot recover from either the creditor or the debtor.

prompt: Atty. Kin obliged himself to paint the portrait of Atty. Con beginning July 26, 2025. They agreed that Atty. Kin will complete the work and effect delivery on Dec. 25, 2026. It was further stipulated that if Atty. Kin failed to fulfill his obligation, he will give his only horse as a penalty. On Dec. 25, 2026, Atty. Kin failed to fulfill his obligation, despite repeated demands from Atty. Con. As a result, which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: The contract between Atty. Kin and Atty. Con need not be in writing to be enforceable
Atty. Con can demand for specific performance plus damages
Atty. Kin is in legal delay and should be required to deliver his only horse plus specific performance and damages
The obligation of Atty. Kin is with a penal clause, hence he is required to give his only horse, which is in lieu of interest and damages, and Atty. Kin can be compelled to paint Atty. Con's portrait

rationale: A penal clause substitutes for indemnity for damages and the payment of interest only when there is no stipulation to the contrary (Art. 1226). Since the horse was expressly agreed to be 'in lieu of interest and damages' only — not in lieu of the principal undertaking — Atty. Con may still compel specific performance of the portrait plus recover the penalty.

prompt: In which of the following cases, will the debtor still enjoy the benefit of the period?

choices.text: If the debtor fails to give the guaranty or security which he promised.
If the guaranty or security is impaired through the fault of the debtor.
If the guaranty or security is lost due to a fortuitous event
If the debtor will go to a foreign country for medical

rationale: Under Art. 1198, the debtor loses the benefit of the period only in specific instances: insolvency, failure to furnish promised security, impairment of security through the debtor's own fault, loss of security through fortuitous event, violation of an undertaking, or absconding. Travelling abroad for medical treatment is not among these grounds, so the debtor keeps the benefit of the period.

prompt: If S a minor sells the necklace of her mother with her mother's consent, to her classmate B, who is also a minor, the contract is

choices.text: Rescissible, and can be rescinded by the parents of her classmate
Valid and effective but the parents of her classmate can ask for annulment.
Unenforceable, unless the parents of buyer B ratify the contract.
Voidable but either S or her mother can ask for annulment

rationale: A contract entered into by a minor is voidable, not void — it remains valid and binding until annulled (Arts. 1327, 1390). Only the party for whose protection incapacity was established, here the minor-buyer's parents, may bring the action for annulment; the seller-minor's side (already consented to by her mother) has no separate right to rescind.

prompt: On Feb 7, 2026 Atty. Per agreed to give to Atty. Tis his only cock if Atty. Tis will pass the CPALE. If the cock will have fruits on May 30, 2026 and Atty. Tis passed the CPALE, where the results were released on May 30, 2026, which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: Atty. Tis has the right to the cock beginning Feb. 7, 2026
Atty. Tis has the right to the fruits beginning May 30, 2026
Atty. Tis will have the right to the cock of Atty. Per on Feb 7, 2026 but not its fruits before May 30, 2026.
The fulfillment of the condition retroacts on the day the contract was perfected making Atty. Tis entitled to the cock and its fruits beginning Feb 7, 2026

rationale: Under Art. 1187, once a suspensive condition is fulfilled, the effects of an obligation to give retroact to the day of the constitution of the obligation. Since the contract was perfected on Feb. 7, 2026 and the condition (passing the CPALE) was later fulfilled, Atty. Tis is deemed entitled to both the cock and its fruits as of Feb. 7, 2026, not only from the date of fulfillment.

prompt: If the consignation was already approved by the court but the debtor thereafter was able to withdraw the money from the court, which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: Such withdrawal was with the consent of the creditor
The obligation of the debtor is revived
The obligation of the co-debtor, guarantor or surety is, revived
The expenses of consignation shall be borne by the

rationale: Under Art. 1260, before the creditor accepts the consignation or before a judicial declaration that it was properly made, the debtor may withdraw the deposit, and the obligation is revived. However, per Art. 1261, once the creditor authorizes such withdrawal after the consignation was already judicially approved, the co-debtors, guarantors, and sureties who were released by the original consignation remain released — they are not revived, making statement (c) incorrect.

prompt: April maintains savings and time deposit amounting to 600k and P1m respectively with Banco de Plata which was closed by the BSP due to alleged fraud and irregularity resulting to bankruptcy. April can demand payment from PDIC amounting to how much?

choices.text: Nothing

rationale: Under the PDIC Charter as amended (RA 11840), the Maximum Deposit Insurance Coverage (MDIC) is ₱1,000,000 per depositor per bank. Since April's savings and time deposits are both single (individual) accounts under her own name in the same closed bank, they are combined for insurance purposes and capped at the ₱1,000,000 MDIC, even though her actual total deposits reach ₱1.6 million.

prompt: Using the same facts in no. 8 but the savings deposit is a joint account with her sister Max, and the time deposit is with her friends, June, July and August. How much can April recover from PDIC?

choices.text: Nothing

rationale: Joint accounts are insured separately from single accounts and are presumed owned equally by each named co-depositor absent a contrary agreement on record with the bank. April's half-share in the joint savings account with Max (½ of ₱600,000 = ₱300,000) plus her one-fourth share in the joint time deposit with June, July, and August (¼ of ₱1,000,000 = ₱250,000) are each within the ₱1,000,000 MDIC cap and are therefore both fully insured, totaling ₱550,000.

prompt: January deposits ₱2m by way of savings deposit with PNB, which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: There exists a contract of loan between January and PNB
PNB became the owner of the ₱2m
PNB is the debtor of the ₱2m
PNB should keep the money safely and return the same money upon demand by January

rationale: A bank deposit — savings, time, or current — is governed by the law on simple loan or mutuum (Art. 1980, NCC), not deposit in the technical sense. The bank acquires ownership of the money and becomes a debtor obligated to return an equivalent amount on demand, not the very same bills/coins deposited — making statement (d) the incorrect one.

prompt: If the right of the creditor to demand payment from the debtor has prescribed because of the passage of time and later payment is effected, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: If payment is effected by a third person, such third person can recover the amount paid
If the payment is effected by the debtor, such debtor can recover the amount paid
If payment is effected by a third person, such third person can recover up to the amount that the debtor was benefited
If the payment is effected by the debtor, such debtor cannot recover the amount paid

rationale: A prescribed debt is not extinguished as a natural obligation — only the civil action to enforce it is barred (Art. 1112 et seq.), and Art. 1423 authorizes the creditor to retain what is voluntarily paid on such a debt. Consequently, a debtor who pays a debt he could no longer be judicially compelled to pay cannot recover what he voluntarily delivered.

prompt: Which of the following contracts is valid but specific performance cannot be sought?

choices.text: Bon agreed to kill Con and if Bon fails, Bon will give ₱2m to Don
Em will give ₱2m to Fe, if Fe will have sex with Em
Roy agreed to paint the house of Eve or if Roy wants Roy will have sex with Cris for one week
Wil agreed to burn the house of Joy and if Wil fails he will pay Joy ₱2m

rationale: This is a facultative obligation where Roy, as debtor, has the option to substitute an accessory prestation (sex, which is void for being contrary to morals) for the valid principal prestation (painting the house). Under Art. 1206, the nullity of the substitution does not invalidate the valid principal obligation, so the contract subsists — but because it is an obligation to do (a personal act), it cannot be enforced through literal specific performance (nemo potest praecise cogi ad factum); the remedy is execution at the debtor's expense (Art. 1167) or damages. The other choices involve a principal object that is itself criminal (murder, arson) or founded on an immoral condition, rendering those entire contracts void under Art. 1409.

prompt: Bato and Coco are solidary debtors of Wawa, Zaza and Yaya, solidary creditors for ₱12,000. Later Wawa condoned the share of Bato, without the knowledge of Yaya and Zaza. On due date, Yaya can collect from

choices.text: Coco only ₱6,000
Either Bato or Coco ₱6,000
Either Bato or Coco ₱8000
Either Coco or Wawa ₱6000

rationale: Under Arts. 1215 and 1219, remission by one solidary creditor of a debtor's obligation binds only that creditor's own undivided interest in the credit — it does not extinguish the shares pertaining to the non-consenting solidary creditors. Since Wawa's condonation of Bato bound only Wawa's own share, Zaza and Yaya may still proceed solidarily against either Bato or Coco for the balance of the debt still owed to them.

prompt: Bobo, Coco or Dodo are solidary debtors of Soso and Toto, solidary creditors for ₱12,000 later Soso, who is courting Dodo, condoned the entire obligation of the debtors, without the knowledge of Toto. One day later, Toto accepted the tender of payment amounting to ₱12,000 made by Bobo without the knowledge of Soso. As a result,

choices.text: Bobo can recover ₱4,000 each from Coco and Dodo
Bobo cannot recover from anyone because the payment was made after the condonation was made
Bobo can recover ₱6,000 from Toto and ₱6,000 from Soso
Toto can recover ₱6,000 from Soso

rationale: A solidary creditor may condone the entire obligation, extinguishing it as to all the solidary debtors, but under Art. 1219 the remitting creditor (Soso) becomes answerable to the other solidary creditor (Toto) for the latter's share of the credit. Because Toto, unaware of Soso's remission, validly accepted Bobo's tender covering the full amount, Toto in effect collected Soso's share as well and must account for it — Soso, not the debtors, bears that loss and Toto may recover Soso's share from Soso.

prompt: The following contracts will take effect upon perfection of the contract, except

choices.text: Emptio rei speratio
Ratification of unenforceable contracts
Fulfillments of suspensive condition
Sale of future things

rationale: As a rule, contracts take effect from the moment of perfection (Art. 1315), including ratification of unenforceable contracts (retroacts) and fulfillment of a suspensive condition (retroacts to perfection under Art. 1187). A sale of 'future things' (emptio rei speratae) is validly perfected at once, but being conditional on the thing coming into existence, its efficacy/demandability — not perfection — is deferred until the future thing actually exists, distinguishing it from the other choices.

prompt: Bubot, a 16 years old student took the watch of her Father with a FMV of ₱20,000 and sold it to Guro, her teacher for only ₱12,000 resulting to a lesion of more than 1/4 of its value, The contract is

choices.text: Voidable, hence her father can ask for annulment
Rescissible, hence her father should ask for rescission within four years
Valid and enforceable
Without effect, unless her father

rationale: A sale where the lesion suffered by one party exceeds one-fourth of the value of the thing sold, entered into by a minor through a guardian/parent's authority, falls under rescissible contracts (Art. 1381). Because the contract causes this specific kind of economic prejudice, the remedy is rescission (accion rescisoria) brought by the party prejudiced (or the parent on the minor's behalf) within four years, not annulment.

prompt: Bebe works as sales clerk in a Boutique store with a daily wage of ₱800. Bebe is scheduled to work on May 1. How much will she receive if the works on that day?
rationale: Under the Labor Code's holiday pay rules, an employee who works on a regular holiday (here, ordinarily 100% of daily wage even if unworked, plus premium if worked) is entitled to 200% of his/her daily rate for the first eight hours worked on that day: ₱800 × 200% = ₱1,600.

prompt: If a minimum wage earner works on this day, she will get a compensation equivalent to 200% of her regular rate

choices.text: Ninoy Aquino day
Manuel L. Quezon day
Andres Bonifacio day
Emilio Aguinaldo day

rationale: Andres Bonifacio Day (November 30) and Rizal Day are 'regular holidays' under the Labor Code; a minimum wage earner who works on a regular holiday receives 200% of the daily rate for the first eight hours, distinguishing it from special (non-working) holidays which carry only a 30% premium.

prompt: Mimi, a cashier who receives ₱800.00 as her daily wage was required to render 6 hours of overtime work from 6pm to 12pm. How much will she receive for that day?
rationale: For overtime work rendered during the employee's night shift differential hours (10pm–6am) on an ordinary day, the employee is entitled to her basic hourly rate plus the 25% overtime premium, further increased by the 10% night differential premium for hours falling within 10pm–6am; computed across the 6-hour overtime stint from 6pm to 12am (with 2 hours falling within the night differential window), the total for the day comes to ₱1,575.00.

prompt: Ada has availed of her 105-day maternity leave with pay. If she wants to extend her leave further, how many days of additional maternity leave, can she availed of?

choices.text: 15 days without pay
30 days without pay
30 days with pay
15 days without pay

rationale: Under the Expanded Maternity Leave Law (RA 11210), a female worker is entitled to 105 days of paid maternity leave (120 days for solo parents), extendible by an additional 30 days without pay at her option, simply upon giving the employer written notice.

prompt: Which of the following is a covered institution under the AMLA

choices.text: Rustan's Dep't Store
Puregold
Tambunting Pawnshop
SM Supermarket

rationale: Under the AMLA (RA 9160, as amended) and its implementing rules, pawnshops are expressly enumerated as covered institutions subject to AMLC reporting requirements, unlike ordinary retail/grocery establishments (Rustan's, Puregold, SM Supermarket), which are not covered persons under the law.

prompt: What is the consequence of being placed on the AMLC's freeze order?

choices.text: Suspension of business permits
Immediate confiscation of assets
Temporary freezing of accounts
Issuance of warrants of arrest

rationale: A freeze order under the AMLA is a provisional remedy issued by the Court of Appeals that temporarily freezes (prevents any transaction, withdrawal, or transfer involving) the monetary instrument or property related to an unlawful activity, pending investigation — it does not itself confiscate assets, suspend permits, or authorize an arrest.

prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: A contract which is without effect is considered ratified by the acceptance by a party to the contract of a benefit under its terms
A contract of marriage between a minor and a deaf mute is valid if made with the consent of their respective parents
The defense of due diligence in the selection and supervision of employees may be used against subsidiary liability of an employer arising from delict.
In culpa contractual, proof of existence of contract and of its breach is sufficient prima facie to warrant recovery

rationale: In culpa contractual (breach of contract), the mere proof of the existence of the contract and the fact of its breach gives rise to a presumption of fault on the part of the party who did not perform, shifting the burden to that party to prove otherwise — this is the accurate statement, while the other choices misstate the rules on ratification of void contracts, capacity to marry, and an employer's subsidiary (not direct) liability for an employee's crime.

prompt: Which of the following statements is wrong?

choices.text: In culpa aquiliana, the source of liability is the defendant's negligent act or omission itself
Concealment or the failure to disclose facts when there is duty to reveal them, as when the parties are bound by confidential relations, constitutes fraud
The statute of frauds does not apply to both partially and wholly executed contracts
A contract of sale between a minor and an insane person is valid and enforceable

rationale: A contract of sale requires both parties to have capacity to give consent; a sale between a minor and an insane person is not validly perfected as to either party's consent and is voidable (or unenforceable, depending on the incapacity), not valid and enforceable as stated — making (d) the incorrect (wrong) statement the question calls for.

prompt: Which of the following contracts is a real contract? Contract

choices.text: To lend a car for one month
To make a deposit of goods
To make a pledge of necklace
Of loan amounting to ₱1m

rationale: A contract of loan (mutuum), like deposit and pledge, is a real contract that is perfected only upon delivery of the object of the contract (Art. 1934, 1963, 2093) — unlike a lease, which is a consensual contract perfected by mere consent even before delivery of the car.

prompt: Ken cleans the house of Tok, in return Ken expects that Tok will clean his condo unit. This is

choices.text: Do ut Des
Do ut Facias
Facio ut Des
Facio ut Facias

rationale: In Roman law classifications of causa still used descriptively in Philippine civil law, 'facio ut facias' denotes 'I do that you may do' — an exchange of services for services, exactly describing Ken's cleaning of Tok's house in exchange for Tok's reciprocal cleaning of Ken's unit.

prompt: Jose, a waiter borrowed ₱200k from his employer Starmoon Coffee. To guarantee the payment, he gave his TCT (transfer certificate of title) to his employer for Starmoon Coffee to hold it until he pays the amount borrowed. There is a contract of

choices.text: Pledge
Real Estate Mortgage
Antichresis
Simple loan

rationale: Where a debtor delivers a certificate of title (a document representing but not constituting delivery of the immovable itself) merely to be held by the creditor as security, without transferring possession of the property or its fruits, the arrangement remains a simple loan with the title held only as additional security, not a real security contract like pledge, mortgage, or antichresis, which each require their own specific formalities and subject matter.

prompt: If a debtor gives a property to his creditor who accepts it in payment of an obligation in money, this will be governed by law on

choices.text: Barter
Cession
Sales
Application of payment

rationale: Dacion en pago (Art. 1245) — giving a thing to satisfy a monetary debt — is governed by the law on sales, with the debt extinguished being treated as the equivalent of the purchase price and the property given as the object sold.

prompt: It is a contract by virtue of the terms of which the parties thereto promise and obligate themselves to enter into another contract at a future time, upon happening of certain events, or the fulfillment of certain conditions

choices.text: Option contract
Arras
Aleatory contract
Resolutory contract

rationale: This describes a bilateral preparatory contract commonly called a contract to sell or, more precisely here, a promise to enter into a future contract — in Philippine civil law terminology this is captured by Art. 1479's option contract framework when unilateral, but a mutual promise to enter into a future contract upon a condition is classified as an option-type preparatory contract, distinguished from arras (earnest money), aleatory contracts (dependent on chance), and resolutory conditions (which extinguish rather than create obligations).

prompt: Maja obliged herself to give Rot ₱1m but if Maja fails, she will have sex with Rot. The contract is

choices.text: Valid, hence Maja has the obligation to give Rot ₱1m
Valid, hence Maja can be compelled to have sex with Rot if she fails to give the ₱1m
Facultative, where the principal is valid but the substitute is not possible
Void, hence Rot cannot demand anything from Maja

rationale: Where an obligation to give a sum of money (₱1M) is coupled with an alternative that is immoral or against public policy (sex), the void alternative does not taint the valid principal obligation; Maja remains bound to give the ₱1M, and the immoral alternative simply cannot be demanded or substituted by either party.

prompt: What is the nature of proceedings under the Financial Rehabilitation and Insolvency Act (FRIA) as described?

choices.text: In Personam, requiring direct notice to all creditors.
In Rem, with jurisdiction acquired through publication.
Criminal proceedings, focusing on debtor misconduct.
Arbitration, requiring mutual agreement among parties

rationale: Proceedings under the Financial Rehabilitation and Insolvency Act (RA 10142) are in rem — jurisdiction over all creditors, known or unknown, is acquired through publication of the commencement order, dispensing with the need for personal notice to each creditor.

prompt: Who is considered an 'individual debtor' under the Financial Rehabilitation and Insolvency Act (FRIA)?

choices.text: Any natural person, regardless of residency or citizenship, has become insolvent.
A corporation that has filed for bankruptcy.
A natural person who is a resident and citizen of the Philippines and has become insolvent.
A foreign national residing in the Philippines

rationale: Under FRIA, an 'individual debtor' is limited to a natural person who is both a resident and a citizen of the Philippines who has become insolvent as defined by the Act — corporations and non-resident/non-citizen individuals fall under different classifications and proceedings under the law.

prompt: Rafael enters a contract with Miguel to sell him the entire mango harvest from his farm for P50,000. The contract is made in January, and the harvest is expected in June. Unfortunately, in May, a severe typhoon destroyed all the mango trees on Rafael's farm, resulting in no harvest. In this case –

choices.text: Rafael is obligated to deliver the mangoes or pay damages to Miguel for non-fulfilment of the obligation.
Rafael can substitute the mangoes with another fruit on his farm to fulfill the obligation.
The contract is valid.
The contract is

rationale: A contract for the sale of a future, expected harvest (emptio rei speratae) is a valid contract from perfection, but since the object is a hoped-for thing that may or may not come into existence, the entire loss of the harvest through a fortuitous event (the typhoon) before it comes into existence extinguishes the obligation without liability to either party — Rafael is not liable for damages nor obligated to substitute or deliver anything.

prompt: Incorporeal property may be delivered by –

choices.text: Mere pointing
Execution of public instrument
Symbolic delivery
Cannot be delivered because it has no physical manifestation

rationale: Incorporeal (intangible) property, such as rights and credits, has no physical body capable of manual or symbolic delivery; under Art. 1498, delivery of incorporeal property is effected through the execution of a public instrument, or, where applicable, by placing the relevant titles of ownership in the possession of the vendee.

prompt: What are the functions of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation (PDIC)?

choices.text: Deposit insurer, co-regulator of banks, and receiver/liquidator of closed banks
Lender of last resort, bank regulator, and financial advisor
Investment banker, financial analyst, and auditor
Bank supervisor, monetary policy maker, and financial market regulator

rationale: The PDIC performs a tripartite function under its Charter: it is the statutory deposit insurer, a co-regulator of banks (jointly with the BSP for safety and soundness examinations), and the statutory receiver and liquidator of closed banks — it is not a monetary authority, lender of last resort, or investment bank.

prompt: Under the principle of Negotiorum Gestio, what is the specific standard of diligence required of the officious manager?

choices.text: Extraordinary diligence
Diligence of a father of a good family
Diligence of a good father of a family
Slight diligence

rationale: Under the rules on negotiorum gestio (Art. 2144 et seq.), the officious manager who voluntarily takes charge of another's business or property must exercise the diligence of a good father of a family in its management, and is liable for damages arising from negligence or fault in the performance of that duty.

prompt: Managers A and B voluntarily take over the management of a neglected restaurant. Due to their negligence, the restaurant's equipment is damaged. What is the nature of their liability to the owner?

choices.text: Joint: A and B are only liable for their respective 50% shares of the damage.
Solidary: The owner can demand the full amount of damages from either A or B.
Subsidiary: The owner must first sue the restaurant staff before suing the managers.
None: Since they acted voluntarily, they cannot be held liable for

rationale: Under Art. 2146, if two or more persons undertake the management of another's business or property jointly (as officious managers), their liability to the owner for the resulting damage from their negligence is solidary, entitling the owner to recover the full amount from either manager.

prompt: If a person is injured, but their own negligence was the 'immediate and proximate' (main) cause of the injury, what happens?

choices.text: They can still get full payment for damages.
They cannot recover any damages at all.
The court will give them double the money.
The defendant must pay even if it wasn't their

rationale: Under the doctrine reflected in Art. 2179, if the plaintiff's own negligence was the immediate and proximate cause of his injury, he cannot recover damages at all; this is distinguished from contributory negligence (where the plaintiff's negligence was only contributory, not the proximate cause), which merely mitigates but does not bar recovery.

prompt: What does an employer need to prove regarding 'Diligence in Selection' to avoid liability for a quasidelict committed by an employee?

choices.text: That they paid the employee a very high salary.
That they are friends with the employee's family.
That they carefully checked the employee's background, skills, and character before hiring them.
That the employee has a university

rationale: To be relieved of vicarious/subsidiary liability for a quasi-delict committed by an employee, the employer must prove observance of the diligence of a good father of a family both in the selection (background, qualifications, and character screening before hiring) and supervision of the employee — mere generosity, friendship, or an employee's academic credentials, standing alone, do not satisfy this burden.

prompt: What is an 'indeterminate' or 'generic' thing?

choices.text: A specific ring with the owner's name engraved on it.
A thing that is designated only by its class or genus
A house located at 123 Maple Street.
A specific painting by Fernando

rationale: A generic or indeterminate thing is one designated only by its kind or class (e.g., '100 bags of cement,' 'a car') without particular individuality, as distinguished from a specific or determinate thing identified by its individuating features (a named ring, a specific address, a particular painting).

prompt: If a debtor fails to deliver 100 bags of cement (a generic thing), what can the creditor do under the law?

choices.text: The creditor must cancel the contract immediately.
The creditor can ask a third person to deliver the cement and charge the cost to the debtor.
The creditor can only sue for 'emotional distress.'
The creditor must wait forever for the debtor to find the

rationale: Where the object of the obligation is generic and the debtor fails to deliver, Art. 1165 (in relation to Art. 1167 for obligations to do) allows the creditor to have the obligation performed by a third person at the debtor's expense, since a generic thing can be sourced from any member of its class and the debtor is not excused merely for personal inability to deliver.

prompt: A debtor promised to deliver his only laptop to 'Person A' on Monday. He also promised to deliver the exact same laptop to 'Person B' on Tuesday. On Wednesday, a lightning strike destroyed the laptop. Is the debtor liable?

choices.text: No, because lightning is a fortuitous event and it is nobody's fault.
Yes, because he promised the same thing to two different persons with different interests.
No, because he hasn't delivered it to anyone yet.
Yes, but only if Person A and Person B are

rationale: In an obligation to deliver a specific (determinate) thing that the debtor bound himself to deliver to two or more persons who do not have the same interest, the debtor's fault in incurring double liability is presumed; he does not enjoy the ordinary rule releasing a debtor of a determinate thing lost through a fortuitous event, since his own act of promising the same unique thing to two parties is itself considered a form of fault under Art. 1165 in relation to the rules on determinate things owed to several creditors.

prompt: If a creditor accepts the full payment of the principal amount without saying anything about the unpaid interest, what does the law generally assume?

choices.text: The creditor has donated the interest to the debtor.
The interest has already been paid.
The interest is still owed and must be paid later.
The contract is automatically

rationale: Under Art. 1253, if a debt produces interest, payment of the principal shall not be deemed made until the interest has been covered; conversely, receipt by the creditor of the principal without reservation as to the interest, when the latter is due, gives rise to a presumption that the interest has been paid.

prompt: What is the general rule regarding rights acquired from an obligation?

choices.text: They can never be transferred to another person.
They are transmissible to others.
They can only be transferred if the debtor gives permission.
They expire the moment the creditor

rationale: As a general rule, rights acquired under an obligation are transmissible, subject to exceptions where the law, the stipulation of the parties, or the nature of the obligation itself provides otherwise (Art. 1178) — intransmissibility is the exception, not the rule.

prompt: In which of the following obligations will delay not exist?

choices.text: Positive obligation
Negative obligation
Personal obligation
Real obligation

rationale: Delay (mora) has no application to negative obligations (obligations not to do); a debtor who is obliged not to do something violates the obligation the moment he performs the prohibited act, at which point there is breach, not delay — delay presupposes a positive obligation still capable of being performed late.

prompt: Which of the following is considered a civil fruit?

choices.text: Young of animal
Palay
Dividend
Grass

rationale: Civil fruits are those derived from a thing by reason of a juridical relation, such as rents of buildings, the price of leases, and dividends from shares of stock (Art. 442) — as distinguished from natural fruits (spontaneous produce of the earth, young of animals) and industrial fruits (produce of land through cultivation, like palay).

prompt: They include everything which is produced by a thing, or which is incorporated or attached thereto, either naturally or

choices.text: Alluvium
Accessions
Accessories
Avulsion

rationale: Accessions are everything produced by, or incorporated/attached to, a thing, whether naturally or artificially (Art. 440), encompassing both accessions discreta (fruits) and accessions continua (buildings, plantings, alluvium, etc.) — broader than 'accessories,' which are things joined to a principal for its use, and distinct from alluvium or avulsion, which are specific modes of accession by water action.

prompt: It refers to a right that can be exercised against the whole world thereby allowing an action to recover the ownership or possession of a specific thing regardless of the possessor of such

choices.text: Personal right
Real right
Intangible right
Tangible right

rationale: A real right (jus in re) is enforceable against the whole world (in rem), allowing its holder to follow the thing and recover it regardless of who possesses it, as distinguished from a personal right (jus in personam), which is enforceable only against a specific obligor.

prompt: D has an outstanding obligation to deliver a specific car to C. If D refuses to deliver the said car to C despite repeated demands, what is the legal remedy available to C?

choices.text: File an action for specific performance plus damages against D
File an action to ask a third person to deliver another car at the expense of D
File an action for annulment of obligation
File an action for reformation of instrument

rationale: Where the object of the obligation is a specific/determinate thing, the creditor may compel the debtor's specific performance of the exact delivery required, in addition to damages for the delay — substitution by another thing at the debtor's expense (a remedy proper to generic obligations) is not available since the thing owed is unique and identified.

prompt: D has an obligation to clean the house of C. If D refused to clean the house of C despite repeated demands, what is the legal remedy available to C?

choices.text: File an action for specific performance plus damages
File an action for annulment of obligation
File an action to ask another person to clean the house or allow D to clean the house at the expense of D
File an action for declaration of nullity of obligation

rationale: An obligation to do (render a service), unlike an obligation to give a determinate thing, cannot be the subject of coercive specific performance compelling the debtor's personal act; instead, if the debtor fails to perform, Art. 1167 allows the creditor to have it executed by another at the debtor's expense, plus damages.

prompt: Which of the following waiver of action is considered valid?

choices.text: Waiver of a civil action for past fraud
Waiver of a civil action for future fraud
Waiver of a civil action for future gross negligence
None of the above

rationale: Under Art. 1171, a waiver of an action to enforce liability arising from fraud is allowed only if the fraud has already been committed (past fraud); a waiver of future fraud, or of future gross negligence (Art. 1171 in relation to Art. 2214/public policy), is void as against public policy, since it would effectively license future bad faith.

prompt: It refers to the right of unpaid creditor to exercise all rights and actions of the judgment debtor to recover his claim, except those rights which are inherently personal to the

choices.text: Accion subrogatoria
Accion pauliana
Accion directa
Accion capcatoria

rationale: Accion subrogatoria (Art. 1177) is the right granted to an unpaid creditor, in the absence of other means to satisfy his claim, to exercise all the rights and bring all the actions of his debtor, except those inherently personal to the debtor — distinguished from accion pauliana (rescission of the debtor's fraudulent alienations) and accion directa (a creditor's direct action against a sub-obligor, as in sub-lease or sub-contract situations).

prompt: Which of the following obligations is not immediately demandable?

choices.text: Pure obligation
Obligation when debtor's means permit him to do so
Obligation with a resolutory period
Obligation with a resolutory condition

rationale: An obligation whose demandability depends upon a future and uncertain event that lies within the debtor's financial capacity ('when his means permit him to do so') is a conditional obligation with a mixed condition and is not immediately demandable, unlike a pure obligation, which is demandable at once, or obligations with a resolutory period/condition, which are demandable at once and only extinguished upon arrival of the period/condition.

prompt: Which of the following suspensive conditions will nullify the obligation that is dependent upon them?

choices.text: Condition purely potestative upon the sole will of debtor
Condition purely potestative upon the sole will of creditor
Mixed condition
Casual condition

rationale: Under Art. 1182, a conditional obligation is void when its fulfillment is made to depend upon a suspensive condition that rests purely and exclusively upon the sole will of the debtor (a purely potestative condition); the same rule does not apply where the potestative condition depends on the creditor's will, or where the condition is mixed or merely casual, which remain valid.

prompt: In conditional reciprocal obligations, what will happen to the fruits and interests during the pendency of the suspensive condition?

choices.text: They shall be forfeited in favor of the state.
They shall inure to the benefit of the debtor.
They shall inure to the benefit of the creditor.
They shall be deemed to have been mutually

rationale: Under Art. 1187 and 1189, during the pendency of a suspensive condition in a reciprocal obligation, the parties are not yet entitled to demand performance, but if the condition is fulfilled, the fruits and interest during the pendency are, as a rule, deemed to have been mutually compensated/offset between the parties (unless the obligation is one to give a determinate thing, in which case Art. 1187 governs fruits received).

prompt: In an alternative obligation, if the contract does not state who has the right to choose which prestation to perform, who holds that right by default?

choices.text: Both parties must agree on the choice together
The Debtor
The Creditor
The Court

rationale: In an alternative obligation, unless the right to choose has been expressly granted to the creditor (or a third person), the right of choice belongs to the debtor as the default rule (Art. 1200).

prompt: What happens if the creditor performs an act that makes it impossible for the debtor to choose between the options in an alternative obligation?

choices.text: The debtor may rescind the contract with damages.
The creditor gets to choose for the debtor.
The debtor must still perform the remaining options regardless of the interference.
The obligation is automatically cancelled without any

rationale: Under Art. 1203, if the party who does not have the right of choice (here, the creditor, since the debtor holds it by default) renders it impossible for the debtor to choose by his own acts, the debtor may rescind the contract, with damages, since the creditor's interference frustrated the debtor's statutory right of election.

prompt: What is the effect if a solidary debtor pays the entire obligation after it has already 'prescribed' (expired due to time)?

choices.text: The other co-debtors must still pay their shares to the one who paid.
The paying debtor loses the right to be reimbursed by the co-debtors.
The creditor must return the money to the debtor.
The co-debtors must pay double because the debt was

rationale: A solidary debtor who, after the debt has already prescribed (and is therefore a mere natural obligation no longer legally demandable), nonetheless pays the entire obligation, is deemed to have made a payment he was not legally compelled to make; consistent with the rule that one who pays a prescribed debt cannot even recover from the original creditor, such a paying debtor likewise loses the right to seek reimbursement from his co-debtors for their shares.

prompt: What is required for a creditor to demand the penalty stipulated in an obligation with a penal clause?

choices.text: The creditor must prove that the debtor acted with malice or fraud.
The creditor must present receipts proving the exact amount of loss.
The creditor only needs to prove that the debtor breached the obligation.
The creditor must first ask the court to calculate the damages.

rationale: Under Art. 1226, in obligations with a penal clause, proof of actual damages is dispensed with — the creditor need only prove the fact of the debtor's breach of the principal obligation to be entitled to demand the stipulated penalty, unless the penalty itself is subject to reduction for being iniquitous or unconscionable.

prompt: Which of the following would be considered a third person 'who has an interest' in the fulfillment of the obligation?

choices.text: A random stranger who wants to be generous.
A guarantor.
A neighbor of the creditor.
None of the above

rationale: Under Art. 1302 (in relation to legal subrogation) and the rules on payment by a third person, a person 'with an interest in the fulfillment of the obligation' refers to someone who would suffer a direct legal or financial prejudice if the obligation is not extinguished, such as a guarantor or surety who is himself liable for the debt — unlike a mere stranger or neighbor who has no such stake.

prompt: In a dation in payment, the debtor transfers ownership of a determinate thing to the creditor to satisfy a debt in money. Which of the following statements regarding its governing law is correct?

choices.text: It is governed primarily by the law on donations since the creditor receives property.
It is governed by the law on sales because the debt is considered the purchase price and the property is the object.
It is governed by the law on agency because the creditor acts as an agent to sell the property.
It is governed by the law on partnerships because the parties share in the value of the property.

rationale: Dacion en pago involves the debtor conveying ownership of a determinate thing to satisfy a pre-existing monetary obligation; by express provision (Art. 1245) and settled jurisprudence, it is governed by the law on sales, with the amount of the debt being extinguished treated as the purchase price and the property delivered as the thing sold.

prompt: Dation in payment and a Contract of Sale share many characteristics. However, they differ in one of the following aspects. Which is it?

choices.text: In a sale, an obligation is created; in dation, an existing obligation is extinguished.
In a sale, there is a transfer of ownership; in dation, there is no transfer of ownership.
In a sale, the cause is a price certain in money; in dation, the cause is the liberality (generosity) of the debtor.
A sale is a real contract, while dation is a consensual contract.

rationale: The fundamental distinction between dacion en pago and an ordinary sale is that in a sale, an obligation is created (the buyer's obligation to pay the price), whereas in dacion en pago, an already-existing obligation is what is being extinguished by the delivery of the property in lieu of money — both remain governed by the law on sales in other respects (e.g., requirement of consent, cause, and object, and both being consensual and involving transfer of ownership).

prompt: D borrowed ₱10,000 from C at an annual interest rate of 10%. On the due date, the total debt is ₱11,000 (₱10,000 principal + ₱1,000 interest). If D pays C ₱5,000 without any specific agreement on how it should be applied, how will the payment be legally credited?

choices.text: The entire ₱5,000 will be applied to the principal, leaving ₱1,000 interest unpaid.
₱2,500 will be applied to the principal and ₱2,500 to the interest.
The payment will first cover the ₱1,000 interest, and the remaining ₱4,000 will be applied to the principal.
The payment is void because it does not cover the full amount of the principal.

rationale: Under Art. 1253, if the debt produces interest, payment of the principal is not deemed made until the interest due has first been covered; applying this rule, D's ₱5,000 payment is first applied to the ₱1,000 interest, with the remaining ₱4,000 credited to the principal.

prompt: If a creditor voluntarily delivers a private document evidencing a debt to the debtor, what is the legal implication?

choices.text: It implies that the debt has been fully paid in cash.
It implies the renunciation of the action the creditor had against the debtor.
It implies that the creditor is appointing the debtor as his new agent.
It has no legal effect unless a public instrument is executed.

rationale: Under Art. 1271, the voluntary delivery by the creditor to the debtor of a private document evidencing the credit implies the renunciation of the creditor's cause of action against the debtor (a presumption of remission of the debt), unless the debtor proves the delivery was made for some other reason.

prompt: What is the effect of confusion (merger of the characters of creditor and debtor) in a joint obligation?

choices.text: The entire obligation is extinguished for all parties involved.
The obligation is extinguished only as regards the share corresponding to the specific person in whom the two characters concur.
The obligation remains fully demandable from the remaining joint debtors by the remaining joint creditors.
The joint obligation is automatically converted into a solidary

rationale: In a joint (as opposed to solidary) obligation, if the characters of creditor and debtor merge in one and the same joint debtor (confusion), the obligation is extinguished only as to that particular joint debtor's own proportionate share, since joint obligations are treated as though there were as many distinct debts as there are debtors/creditors (Art. 1208, in relation to Art. 1275).

prompt: When can debts that are rescissible or voidable be compensated against each other?

choices.text: Before they are judicially rescinded or avoided.
Only if both parties explicitly waive their right to sue for rescission.
Never, because these debts are considered defective from the beginning.
Only after a judge has confirmed the validity of both

rationale: Under Art. 1290, debts which are rescissible or voidable may be validly compensated against each other before they have been judicially rescinded or avoided, since until such judicial declaration, these contracts remain valid and produce all their legal effects.

prompt: Under Article 1287, which of the following debts is strictly prohibited from being extinguished by legal compensation?

choices.text: debt arising from a depositum or the obligations of a depositary.
A debt arising from an lease agreement.
A debt arising from a simple loan (mutuum) with interest.
A debt arising from a contract of

rationale: Under Art. 1287, compensation cannot take place against a depositary's or bailee's obligation to return the specific thing deposited, out of respect for the trust nature of a depositum (and similarly, obligations of a bailee in commodatum) — the law does not allow such obligations to be extinguished merely by an offsetting debt.

prompt: In a case of 'delegacion,' where the original debtor proposes a new debtor to the creditor, what is the general rule if the new debtor becomes insolvent after the substitution?

choices.text: The creditor can automatically go back to the original debtor to demand payment.
The action of the creditor against the original debtor is NOT revived.
The original debtor must pay half of the debt to show good faith.
The obligation is extinguished for everyone, and the creditor loses the

rationale: Under Art. 1295, if the new debtor substituted in a delegacion becomes insolvent, the creditor's action against the original debtor is revived only if the insolvency was already existing and of public knowledge, or known to the original debtor, at the time he delegated his debt; as a general rule absent these circumstances, the action against the original debtor is NOT revived.

prompt: As a rule, what happens to the original obligation if the new obligation intended to novate it is void?

choices.text: The parties must create a third obligation to replace both.
The original obligation is extinguished along with the void new one.
The debtor is released from all liability as a penalty to the creditor.
The original obligation subsists and remains

rationale: As a general rule under Art. 1298, if the new obligation intended to substitute (novate) an old one is void, the original obligation subsists and remains in force, since a void novation produces no legal effect and cannot extinguish a valid pre-existing obligation.

prompt: Legal subrogation is presumed when a creditor pays another creditor who is 'preferred.' Does this subrogation require the debtor's knowledge or consent?

choices.text: Yes, but only if the preferred creditor is a banking institution.
No, but it only applies if the debtor is currently in default (mora).
No, it takes place even without the debtor's knowledge.
Yes, the debtor must give express consent for the transfer of credit

rationale: Under Art. 1302(2), legal subrogation takes place, by operation of law and without need of the debtor's knowledge or consent, when a creditor pays another creditor who is preferred, by reason of a mortgage, pledge, or other lien.

prompt: When bank records indicate in a deposit account the name of a person followed by the preposition 'by' and the name of another person (e.g., 'Danilo Reyes by Dianne Fernandez'), the maximum insured deposit belongs to:

choices.text: Danilo Reyes
Dianne Fernandez
Both Danilo Reyes and Dianne Fernandez shared equally
The person who physically deposited the money

rationale: Under PDIC rules, a deposit account recorded 'in trust for,' 'by,' or 'for the account of' another (an ITF/'by' account) is deemed owned by, and insured in the name of, the named beneficiary/principal (here, Danilo Reyes) rather than the person who administers or physically deposits the funds (Dianne Fernandez).

prompt: What is the primary purpose of a freeze order under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA)?

choices.text: To allow the bank to use the funds for its own investments during the investigation.
To penalize the account holder for failing to submit a Suspicious Transaction Report.
To permanently confiscate the funds and transfer them to the National Treasury.
To prevent the withdrawal, transfer, or dissipation of funds related to an unlawful

rationale: A freeze order under the AMLA is intended to preserve the status quo by preventing the withdrawal, transfer, removal, dissipation, or disposition of monetary instruments or property related to an unlawful activity or money laundering offense while investigation and forfeiture proceedings are ongoing — it is not a penalty, confiscation, or arrest mechanism.

prompt: What is the quantum of evidence required for the Court of Appeals to issue a freeze order?

choices.text: Proof beyond reasonable doubt
Preponderance of evidence
Probable cause
Substantial evidence

rationale: Under the AMLA's implementing rules, the Court of Appeals may issue a freeze order upon a finding of probable cause that the monetary instrument or property is related to an unlawful activity, a lower quantum than proof beyond reasonable doubt, preponderance of evidence, or substantial evidence.

prompt: Statement 1: Under AMLA, covered persons are prohibited from communicating to any person the fact that a covered transaction report was made, its contents, and other information in relation. Statement 2: Under AMLA, accountants acting as legal independent professionals are required to report covered transactions of the relevant information, although obtained in professional.

choices.text: Both statements are correct
Both statements are incorrect

rationale: Statement 1 correctly describes the 'tipping off' prohibition under Sec. 9(c) of the AMLA, which bars covered persons from disclosing that a covered/suspicious transaction report has been, is being, or will be filed. Statement 2 is incorrect: the AMLA expressly exempts lawyers and accountants acting as independent legal professionals from the reporting requirement as to information they receive from a client in the context of ascertaining the client's legal position or in providing legal advice/representation, in recognition of privileged communications.

prompt: Under the 'Safe Harbor Provision,' no case shall lie against a person for reporting a transaction to the AMLC if:

choices.text: The report leads to a successful conviction.

rationale: The 'Safe Harbor Provision' of the AMLA (Sec. 9(c)) shields covered persons and their officers/employees from criminal, civil, or administrative liability for making a covered or suspicious transaction report, provided it was made in the regular performance of their duties and in good faith, whether or not a suspicious or covered transaction is later confirmed.

prompt: What is the prohibited act of 'Tipping Off' under the AMLA?

choices.text: Sharing AMLC circulars with other bank branches.
Accepting a tip or bribe from a customer to skip KYC procedures.
Reporting a suspicious transaction to the AMLC without the manager's approval.

rationale: The prohibited act of 'tipping off' under the AMLA consists of directly or indirectly disclosing to any person, including the client involved, that a covered or suspicious transaction report has been, is being, or will be reported, or any related information, which would compromise an ongoing investigation.

prompt: Under AMLA, which of the following best defines a 'Beneficial Owner'?

choices.text: Any person who is a registered shareholder in the SEC General Information Sheet.
The bank manager who oversees the corporate account relationship.
The government regulator tasked with monitoring the financial institution

rationale: Under the AMLA and its implementing rules on beneficial ownership, a 'beneficial owner' is the natural person who ultimately owns, controls, or exercises ultimate effective control over a customer, or on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted, looking through any layers of corporate or nominee arrangements — not merely the person listed as a registered shareholder or the institution's own personnel/regulators.

prompt: Are 'Kasambahays' (Domestic Workers) entitled to 13th-month pay under Philippine Law?

choices.text: Yes, but it is purely discretionary on the part of the employer.
Only if the employer has more than 10 employees.
No, they are only entitled to their agreed monthly wage.

rationale: Under DOLE regulations implementing the Batas Kasambahay (RA 10361), a domestic worker who has rendered at least one month of service is entitled to a 13th-month pay equivalent to at least one-twelfth (1/12) of the total basic salary earned within the calendar year, regardless of the number of household employees.

prompt: Which of the following best describes the financial condition of an individual debtor who may file a petition for Suspension of Payments under FRIA?

choices.text: The debtor has no assets and is completely insolvent.
The debtor's liabilities exceed their total assets by at least ₱500,000.
The debtor is a corporation undergoing financial distress.

rationale: Under FRIA, an individual debtor may file a petition for suspension of payments if he possesses sufficient property to cover all his debts but foresees the impossibility of meeting them as they respectively fall due — distinguishing this remedy from insolvency/liquidation, which presupposes that liabilities already exceed assets.

prompt: What is the legal effect(s) of the 'Suspension Order' issued by the court upon the filing of a verified petition?

choices.text: It automatically cancels all of the debtor's debts.
The debtor is required to leave the country until the debts are paid.

rationale: Upon the issuance of a Suspension Order (whether under FRIA's suspension of payments for individuals or the commencement order for corporate rehabilitation), all pending actions for claims against the debtor are suspended and no creditor may sue to collect, except for certain exempted claims (e.g., labor claims for unpaid wages in some contexts) as specifically provided by law — it does not cancel debts outright or compel the debtor to leave the country.
